pl-l4d4c5-d1e115.summary: Asks what baptism confers on those already sanctified by the Spirit who come to it with faith and charity, since it seems to give them nothing, their sins already being remitted through faith and contrition.

pl-l4d4c5-d1e118.summary: Answers that they are justified by faith and contrition, cleansed from sin's stain and absolved from eternal penalty, yet still bound by the temporal satisfaction imposed on penitents in the Church. In baptism they are cleansed of any sins contracted since conversion, absolved from outward satisfaction, and assisting grace and every virtue are increased, so they can truly be called new; the tinder of sin is also further weakened.
claims: The justified still owe temporal satisfaction before baptism.
Baptism absolves them from outward satisfaction and increases grace.
Baptism weakens the tinder of sin.

pl-l4d4c5-d1e121.summary: Cites Jerome: the faith that makes believers is given or nourished in the waters of baptism, given to those without it and increased in those who have it; so too with the other gifts.

pl-l4d4c5.summary: Asks what baptism confers on those already sanctified by the Spirit who come to it with faith and charity, since their sins are already forgiven. They are justified, cleansed of sin's stain and freed from eternal penalty, but still bound to the temporal satisfaction imposed on penitents; in baptism they are cleansed of sins contracted since conversion, released from outward satisfaction, and given increase of assisting grace and every virtue, becoming truly new; the tinder of sin is further weakened. So Jerome says the faith that makes believers is given or nourished in baptism.
claims: Those justified by faith and contrition before baptism still owe temporal satisfaction.
Baptism releases them from outward satisfaction and remits later sins.
Baptism increases grace and virtues and weakens the tinder of sin.
Faith is given or nourished in baptism.
